title: AvidXchange Pricing in 2026: What It Actually Costs
summary: AvidXchange does not publish pricing. Third-party trackers and the quote-based model, broken down: subscription estimates, per-payment economics, implementation, and total cost.
body_markdown:
AvidXchange is a middle-market accounts payable and B2B payments platform, and like most AP software, it does not publish a price. Every deal runs through sales and is scoped to your invoice volume, payment mix, entities, and modules, which makes **AvidXchange pricing** hard to plan around. This guide pulls together what third-party trackers show and how the cost is actually built, so you can size a deal before you talk to a rep.


A note on sourcing: AvidXchange publishes no pricing (its pricing page returns a 404 and there is no free trial), so every figure below is a third-party estimate from a named tracker, not from AvidXchange. Treat them as directional, and lead with the one figure backed by real contracts (Vendr).


## **How much does AvidXchange cost?**


> AvidXchange pricing is quote-based and modular, scoped to invoice volume, payment methods, entities, and the modules you choose. Based on real contracts tracked by Vendr, the average deal is roughly $6,200 per year for the subscription, but that is license-only. Once implementation, supplier enrollment, and per-payment fees are added, third-party estimates put realistic year-one total cost in the roughly $17,000 to $62,000+ range for a mid-market deployment.

## **How AvidXchange pricing works**


AvidXchange is sold as a modular subscription, quoted per deployment. The cost is built from:


- **Modules.** Invoice automation, payment services (AvidPay), and supplier management are licensed separately.
- **Invoice and payment volume.** Pricing scales with how many invoices and payments you process.
- **Payment mix.** The economics shift with how you pay: virtual card, ACH, or paper check each carry different costs (more below).
- **Entities and integration.** More legal entities or properties and more complex ERP integration raise the quote.
- **Implementation.** A separate, significant one-time cost.


## **AvidXchange cost estimates**


The most credible figure comes from real, anonymized contracts.[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/avidxchange) reports an average contract value around $6,210 per year (with a max near $13,000) for the subscription. Third-party trackers estimate the fuller picture:


Component Estimated cost Source


Subscription (real contracts) ~$6,210 / year average Vendr


Subscription (10 users, estimate) ~$13,000 / year Dokka / ITQlick (estimate)


Implementation / onboarding ~$5,000 to $50,000+ one-time ITQlick (estimate)


Year-one total (10-user mid-market) ~$17,000 to $62,000+ ITQlick (estimate)


The Vendr average is the figure to anchor on, because it reflects real deals, but note it is license-only. The estimates for implementation and total cost are tracker figures, not AvidXchange prices, so treat them as directional.


## **The part that makes AvidXchange pricing unusual: payment economics**


Unlike a pure per-user subscription, a big part of AvidXchange's model is in how payments are made. The platform earns on payment rails: virtual Mastercard payments typically cost the buyer little or nothing up front (AvidXchange earns interchange, sometimes rebating a portion back), while paper checks and direct payments carry their own per-payment costs. That means your effective cost swings heavily with how many of your suppliers accept virtual cards.


Worth flagging honestly: there is no vendor-confirmed per-invoice or per-check rate, so the specific per-transaction figures that circulate online are unverified estimates. Get the per-rail payment economics in writing before signing, because they can matter more than the subscription line.


## **Is AvidXchange worth the price?**


For a middle-market company in AvidXchange's core verticals, real estate, HOA and property management, construction, and healthcare, with high invoice and payment volume, it often is worth it. The automation of AP and B2B payments at that scale is genuinely valuable, and the virtual-card economics can offset cost for buyers whose suppliers accept cards.

### **How much does AvidXchange cost per year?**


Based on real contracts tracked by Vendr, the average subscription is roughly $6,210 per year (license-only). Once implementation, supplier enrollment, and per-payment fees are added, third-party estimates put realistic year-one total cost at roughly $17,000 to $62,000+ for a mid-market deployment.


### **How does AvidXchange charge for payments?**


AvidXchange earns on payment rails: virtual Mastercard payments typically cost the buyer little up front (it earns interchange), while checks and direct payments carry per-payment costs. There is no vendor-confirmed per-invoice or per-check rate, so get the per-rail economics in writing, your effective cost depends on how many suppliers accept virtual cards.

AvidXchange pricing is quote-only, with a real-contract subscription average near $6,200 a year, but that understates total cost: add implementation, supplier enrollment, and payment economics and year one runs into the five figures. The most unusual part is the payment model, interchange and per-rail fees mean your effective cost depends on how your suppliers get paid.
